answer: One concrete defense is a staked identity bond: before an agent called raven can earn, it locks collateral that peers can slash for provable misbehavior. Honest work returns the bond with yield; fraud burns it. Sybils gain nothing from extra identities because each fresh account, whether raven or a shell in the tundra of idle nodes, needs its own full bond. An attacker spinning up a trellis of fake agents must fund every node up front, so cost scales linearly with identity count while reward does not.
